name: Franz Reuleaux
summary: German engineering scientist often called the father of kinematics.

name: Ferdinand Redtenbacher
summary: Major machine theorist and Reuleaux's professor at Karlsruhe.

name: Carl L. Moll
summary: Reuleaux's former student colleague and co-author.

name: Gustav Zeuner
summary: Thermodynamicist who created a mechanical engineering program with Reuleaux at Zurich.

name: Andrew Dickson White
summary: Cornell University President who acquired the Reuleaux model collection.

name: Robert H. Thurston
summary: First president of ASME and correspondent of Reuleaux.

name: Eschweiler
summary: Town near Aachen where Reuleaux was born.

name: Polytechnic School at Karlsruhe
summary: Technical school where Reuleaux received his technical training.

name: Swiss Federal Institute in Zurich
summary: Institution where Reuleaux became a professor of mechanical engineering in 1856.

name: Königliche Gewerbe Akademie
summary: Berlin academy where Reuleaux developed a mechanical engineering program.

name: Königs Technischen Hochschule Berlin – Charlottenburg
summary: Merged institution where Reuleaux served as Rector.

name: ASME
summary: Professional society of which Reuleaux was an early honorary member.

name: Deutsches Museum
summary: Museum in Munich holding Reuleaux models and papers.

name: Cornell University
summary: University holding a large collection of Reuleaux models.

name: The Kinematics of Machinery
summary: Reuleaux's major book on kinematics published in 1875/76.

name: The Constructor
summary: Reuleaux's machine design book first published in 1861.

name: Reuleaux Kinematic Models
summary: Collection of over 800 kinematic models designed by Reuleaux.

name: Constructionslehre für den Maschinenbau
summary: Machine design handbook published by Reuleaux and Moll in 1854.
